content: Lysis can be conducted at lower administrative levels, which could potentially allow for earlier declarations of transmission interruption and disease elimination. However, this approach is not recommended because such declarations should be thoroughly assessed by an internal team. Including lower administrative tiers in the assessment process may result in an overwhelming number of evaluations, complicating the process. Dr. Manoj Murhekar, Director of the National Institute of Epidemiology in Chennai, India, presented surveillance indicators used in tuberculosis (TB) control and the recommended process for verifying sub-national claims. The verification process involves reviewing programmatic data, such as TB scores, the number of cases requiring prophylactic treatment to prevent one case, medicine sales data (both public and private), and community-based surveys. The National Tuberculosis Programme has set ambitious targets, including ending TB by 2025. Specific goals include an 80% reduction in TB incidence by 2020 (compared to 2015), a 90% reduction in annual TB deaths by 2030 (compared to 2015), and ensuring no TB-affected households face catastrophic costs by 2020. Impact indicators include reducing estimated TB incidence, prevalence, and mortality rates per 100,000 population, as well as achieving zero catastrophic costs for TB-affected families. Monitoring progress toward a TB-free status at sub-national levels is critical. A system has been initiated to incentivize and reward well-performing districts and states. This includes identifying a fixed number of bacteriologically positive TB cases in each district to estimate TB incidence and underreporting in the notification system (Nikshay). The sampling strategy involves dividing districts into survey units, selecting villages or wards using probability proportional to population size, and enrolling individuals until 30 bacteriologically positive TB cases are identified per district. Community-based surveys use indicators such as the proportion of participants eligible for sputum sample collection, symptomatic individuals, new cases identified during the survey, patients on TB treatment, and individuals with a history of TB after March 2020. Underreporting is assessed by identifying participants currently treated for TB or with a past history of TB not found in Nikshay. Verification of sub-national TB-free claims is based on specific criteria. For example, claims are not recommended if any of the three incidence estimates exceed 10% of the baseline estimate. Claims are supported if two out of three point estimates of decline in incidence align with the claimed category, and no incidence estimate shows an increase from the baseline. Higher-than-claimed categories are supported if two out of three point estimates indicate a greater decline, or if the lower bounds of confidence intervals support a higher category. TB-free status is declared when all three incidence estimates are below 44 per 100,000 population. The distribution of districts and states by TB status in India in 2020 showed varying levels of reduction in TB incidence compared to 2015. Awards were given based on the percentage reduction: Bronze (20-40%), Silver (41-60%), Gold (61-80%), and TB-free (>80%). For leprosy, a Leprosy Transmission Assessment Survey (LTAS) was proposed to ascertain zero leprosy status and announce transmission interruption at the second sub-national level, as well as disease elimination at the national level. LTAS ensures early detection of all cases in the community before deformities develop and transmission occurs among healthy individuals. It involves reviewing epidemiological data, assessing health facilities, validating data through field surveys, and verifying criteria. Epidemiological data review includes analyzing data at the second sub-national level over 10-20 years, such as new child cases and total cases, as applied in countries like Maldives, Morocco, Thailand, and Vietnam. Health facility assessments verify the availability of diagnostic services, staff knowledge and skills, and multidrug therapy (MDT) at facilities treating patients. Care for ulcers or disabilities, stigma reduction measures, and mental health improvement are also evaluated. Field surveys are included in LTAS due to the lack of objective tests to confirm community infection. A sample of contacts, including children and at-risk populations, is checked for leprosy. Sample size calculations for each sub-national unit are determined after discussions with epidemiologists and statisticians. Verification of criteria is conducted by internal teams at the sub-national level when reaching the interruption of transmission stage. LTAS serves as a pre-qualification tool to confirm that a unit has achieved this milestone. When all second-tier sub-national units within a first-tier unit reach interruption of transmission, the first-tier unit is automatically declared to have achieved this status. Similarly, when all first-tier units meet the criteria for disease elimination, the country is considered to have achieved disease elimination. Post-elimination surveillance is maintained for at least ten years to detect sporadic cases. An international team verifies disease elimination at the national level. A Country Dossier, prepared by the country, contains evidence to claim leprosy elimination at the national level. It is submitted to WHO for verification. The dossier includes epidemiological evidence, programmatic criteria, and achievements. Background information, such as geographic and population details, health system organization, and social determinants of health, is also included. Mandatory information about leprosy control activities includes the history of the leprosy program, trends in leprosy, evolution of MDT programs, and other interventions. The dossier also outlines sub-national units assessed, classification of units by endemicity level, and baseline data for trend analysis. National strategic plans, standard operating procedures, resource allocation, and inclusion of partners and affected individuals are detailed. Indicators monitored include input, process, and output indicators, as well as outcomes and results. LTAS exercises carried out at sub-national units are summarized, including protocols, sampling procedures, and detailed reports. Final criteria for verification are described, with data collection formats and verifiable indicators outlined. Countries are encouraged to develop national strategic plans, including standard operating procedures and capacity-building plans to sustain clinical and programmatic expertise. Seroprevalence for anti-M. leprae PGL-I IgM is also considered.
